The Science of LearningContents

EDCOR 310 · Recorded Lectures

Recorded Lectures

Watch every video in the week-by-week course sequence. Use the plus sign for descriptions and the rating controls to tell us what helps.

How this works

Watch every video. Online students should watch every video in this index and keep a brief record of what they are learning.

In-person students. If you are an in-person student, you are expected to be in class. These recordings are an extra resource for review; watching them may not substitute for attendance.

Use the plus. Open a unit, then open a week and a video row to see its description and additional details. Each video opens in a new tab.

Read the tags. BroPa marks an instructor-made recording. Third party marks a video made by someone else or hosted outside the course.

Make time to process. You are welcome to read or watch faster if you choose, but leave time to pause, take notes, connect ideas, and record what you are learning. Speed is useful only when you are still processing the material.

Watch actively. As you watch, record the main claim, the evidence or example behind it, and one idea you could explain in your own words.

About the times. Times are rough estimates for planning only. Every video in this index belongs to the assigned collection.

  • Unit 1: The Holy Art of Skepticism: Principles of Research in Psychology
  • Unit 2: Developmental Psychology: Adventures in Child Psychopathy
  • Unit 3: Motivational Psychology: Why We Do What We Do
  • Unit 4: Cognitive Psychology: How the Brain Learns
